introduction.text: The Amphitheatrum Castrense is a Roman amphitheatre in Rome, adjacent to Santa Croce in Gerusalemme. It is significant as an example of imperial entertainment architecture and its later transformation into a defensive structure within the Aurelian Walls.

history.description: Built by Emperor Elagabalus in the early 3rd century AD as part of the Horti Spei Veteris imperial villa complex.
Arches of the outer walls were bricked up during incorporation into the Aurelian Walls (271–275 AD), ending its use for spectacles.
Mid‑16th‑century demolition of the second story for defensive purposes.
18th‑century discovery of a hypogeum beneath the arena, filled with bones of large animals, indicating venationes.

design.description: Regular ellipse measuring 88 × 76 m, built of brick‑faced concrete with decorative travertine elements.
Three‑story structure, with only the lowest story preserved today.

art.description: Drawings by Andrea Palladio and Étienne Dupérac documented the ruins of the amphitheatre.
